title: 🧠 A player plays GTA 6 with his thoughts alone — a brain chip instead of a controller!
body: 🧠 A player plays GTA 6 with his thoughts alone — a brain chip instead of a controller!

Neuralink published a two-minute video on November 20 showing a participant in its clinical trials playing GTA 6 — released worldwide on November 19 — using a chip implanted in his brain, without touching a controller.

In the clip, the player drives a speedboat under a bridge and through a narrow channel between trees to collect a package, then drives a car, flies a seaplane and gets into a fight — all by imagining small movements of his fingers, hands and feet.

The company's Telepathy system reads activity in the brain area responsible for hand movement and turns the imagined movement into digital commands: imagining a tap with the ring finger, for example, fires a command, and imagining pushing the right hand forward raises the plane's nose.

The video shows a split screen: the player in a corner, a live neural-decoding panel, and a drawing of a PlayStation 5 controller whose buttons light up with each recorded command. The company did not reveal the player's identity or the gaming device used.

The player — who posts under the name "Loperin James" — said the hardest part is remembering dozens of imagined movements, each linked to a different button, adding that before the chip he used a mouth stick and an electronic board. A company engineer developed special software that translates the chip's signals into controller commands.

This is not the company's first gaming experiment: in 2024 its first trial participant played Civilization 6 and Mario Kart the same way. The company's devices remain experimental and have not yet been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration, and game-device control is available to only some participants so far.

Simply put: imagine thinking about moving your finger and the game cursor moves. The chip reads the "I want to move" signal from your brain and translates it into a button pressed on its own — your thoughts become the controller.
Do you think thought control will first change the lives of those who cannot use their hands, or is gaming just a preview of what is coming?
